steps: Select the longest continuous carbon chain as the parent chain.
Name the parent chain using the appropriate carbon-number prefix (such as meth-, eth-, prop- or but-) followed by the suffix “-ane.”
Number the parent chain from the end nearest the first branch.
Name each branch as an alkyl group and show its position by a number.
If the same alkyl group occurs more than once, use di-, tri- or other suitable prefixes and give all its position numbers.
Write the complete name with the position numbers and branch names before the parent-chain name.
items.finalAnswer: An alkane is named using the appropriate carbon prefix for its longest parent chain and the suffix “-ane”; branches are named and numbered as prefixes.
